summary.title: Transformers from Scratch
summary.one_liner: You learn how transformers work by building up from one-hot encodings, dot products and matrix multiplication to Markov chains, masked attention and the QK^T lookup behind the attention equation.
keywords: first order vs second order sequence model
why matrix multiplication for neural networks
takeaways: One-hot vectors plus matrix multiplication act as a differentiable lookup table, which is the core trick transformers rely on.
Markov chains predict the next word from recent words; skip-style features let a model reach back over long gaps by weighting word pairs.
Masking zeroes out uninformative features, and this selective masking is the attention described in the 2017 paper.
Transformers are built from matrix multiplications because they are fast on hardware and must be differentiable and well conditioned for backpropagation.
The QK^T term in the attention equation is a learned, differentiable lookup of masks, and a single-layer ReLU network builds word-pair features.
summary.summary: This long tutorial explains transformers step by step, starting from a toy voice-command interface. It introduces one-hot encoding, dot products and matrix multiplication, then uses them to model word sequences with first and second order Markov chains and a second-order model with skips. The author shows how masking acts as attention and how matrix multiplications can implement lookups, with a hand-built ReLU layer creating word-pair features. The page is partway through; the listing's sections cover the rest (embeddings, softmax, multi-head attention, encoder/decoder stacks), which the captured text does not reach.
